style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The first half of a broken acrostic -- Psalms 9 and 10 run through the Hebrew alphabet together, with gaps, and the Greek Psalter counts them as one psalm. Psalm 9 is the thanksgiving half: David has been vindicated, the enemy has turned back and perished before God's face, cities are uprooted and even their memory is gone, and he sings it with his whole heart. But the psalm keeps widening from his case to the world's: the LORD sat down on the throne to judge David's cause, and the LORD sits enthroned forever to judge the world in righteousness. That Judge is also a high stronghold for the crushed, One who remembers the cry of the afflicted when He audits blood, who does not forget the needy forever. Midway the tense changes -- be gracious to me, see my affliction, You who lift me from the gates of death -- because the vindicated man is still in danger, and he wants to live to tell it in the gates of Zion. The nations sink into their own pit; the wicked return to Sheol; and the psalm ends asking God to teach the empires the one lesson they never learn: they are only human. Higgaion. Selah.

1.text: For the choir director, set to 'The Death of the Son.' A psalm of David. I will give You thanks, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will recount all Your wonders.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Muthlabben, A Psalm [mizmor] of David. I will praise [yadah -- give thanks] You, O LORD [YHWH], with my whole heart [leb]; I will show forth [saphar -- recount, tell] all Your marvellous works [pala -- wonders].
1.notes: odeh YHWH be-khol-libbi (H3034, H3068, H3820): thanks with the WHOLE heart, the first line of an acrostic that runs, with gaps, from aleph here through Psalm 10 -- the two psalms are one poem in the Greek Psalter. asapperah kol-niphleotekha (H5608, H6381): I will RECOUNT Your wonders -- saphar, the counting-verb: praise as an itemized list. Muth-labben (H4192), 'death of the son', is most likely a tune name.

2.text: I will be glad and exult in You; I will make music to Your name, O Most High.
2.amp: I will be glad [samach] and rejoice [alats -- exult] in You: I will sing praise [zamar -- make music] to Your name [shem], O You most High [Elyon].
2.notes: esmechah ve-eeltsah bakh (H8055, H5970): glad and exultant IN You -- the object of the joy is God, not the victory -- azammerah shimkha Elyon (H2167, H8034, H5945): music to the name of Elyon, the Most High, Melchizedek's title for God (Genesis 14:18-20), the name that puts every earthly power below Him.

3.text: When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before Your face.
3.amp: When mine enemies [oyeb] are turned [shub] back [achor], they shall fall [kashal -- stumble] and perish [abad] at Your presence [panim -- face].
3.notes: be-shub-oyebai achor (H7725, H341, H268): the enemies turning tail -- yikkashelu ve-yobedu mi-panekha (H3782, H6, H6440): they stumble and perish FROM YOUR FACE. No sword is mentioned; the presence of God is what routed them (cf. Psalm 68:1-2).

4.text: For You have upheld my right and my cause; You sat down on the throne as a righteous Judge.
4.amp: For You have maintained ['made my judgment', asah mishpat, the KJV margin] my right and my cause [din]; You sat [yashab] in the throne [kisse] judging ['judging in righteousness', shaphat tsedek, the KJV margin] right.
4.notes: asita mishpati ve-dini (H6213, H4941, H1779): the margin's literal, 'You MADE my judgment' -- You produced the verdict I could not get -- yashabta le-khisse shophet tsedek (H3427, H3678, H8199, H6664): You SAT to the throne, the judge taking His seat -- the courtroom picture that runs through the whole psalm. Personal vindication first, then the world's (v. 8).

5.text: You rebuked the nations, You destroyed the wicked; You wiped out their name forever and ever.
5.amp: You have rebuked [gaar] the heathen [goy -- nations], You have destroyed [abad] the wicked [rasha], You have put out [machah -- wiped out, blotted out] their name [shem] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
5.notes: gaarta goyim (H1605, H1471): a rebuke -- the same root whose noun turns back the waters in Psalm 104:7 -- ibbadta rasha (H6, H7563), and shemam machita le-olam va-ed (H8034, H4229, H5769, H5703): their NAME wiped out -- machah, the erasing-verb of the Flood (Genesis 7:23) and of Amalek's memory (Exodus 17:14). The nations' proudest possession, their name, gone; verse 2 has just sung the Name that stays.

6.text: The enemy has come to an end -- ruins forever; You have uprooted their cities, and the very memory of them has perished.
6.amp: O you enemy [oyeb], destructions [chorbah -- ruins] are come to a perpetual [netsach] end [tamam -- finished] ['The destructions of the enemy are come to a perpetual end: and their cities hast thou destroyed', oyeb, the KJV margin]: and You have destroyed cities [ir]; their memorial [zeker -- memory] is perished [abad] with them [hem].
6.notes: ha-oyeb tammu chorabot la-netsach (H341, H8552, H2723, H5331): the enemy -- finished, ruins in perpetuity; the KJV's vocative 'O thou enemy' and its margin's statement are the two ways the Hebrew can be read, and the WEB follows the margin. ve-arim natashta (H5892, H5428): cities UPROOTED, the plant-verb -- abad zikram hemmah (H6, H2143, H1992): their memory has perished -- 'they', the pronoun dangling at the end like a name no one can finish.

7.text: But the LORD sits enthroned forever; He has set up His throne for judgment,
7.amp: But the LORD [YHWH] shall endure [yashab -- sits, remains] for ever [olam]: He has prepared [kun -- established] His throne [kisse] for judgment [mishpat].
7.notes: va-YHWH le-olam yeshev (H3068, H5769, H3427): the LORD SITS forever -- yashab, the sitting of a king on his throne and of a judge on his bench, which the KJV renders 'endure' and the WEB 'reigns'; the contrast is with the vanished cities of verse 6. konen la-mishpat kiso (H3559, H4941, H3678): His throne is set up FOR JUDGMENT -- a courtroom, not a parade stand.

8.text: and He will judge the world in righteousness; He will pass judgment on the peoples with fairness.
8.amp: And He shall judge [shaphat] the world [tebel] in righteousness [tsedek], He shall minister judgment [din] to the people [leom -- peoples] in uprightness [meyshar -- equity].
8.notes: ve-hu yishpot-tebel be-tsedek (H8199, H8398, H6664): the whole inhabited world judged in righteousness -- yadin leummim be-mesharim (H1777, H3816, H4339): the peoples adjudicated with mesharim, level dealing, no thumb on the scale. Psalm 96:13 and 98:9 sing the same line at the LORD's coming; Paul preached it at Athens (Acts 17:31).

9.text: And the LORD will be a high stronghold for the crushed, a high stronghold in times of trouble.
9.amp: The LORD [YHWH] also will be a refuge ['an high place', misgab, the KJV margin] for the oppressed [dak -- crushed], a refuge [misgab -- high stronghold] in times [et] of trouble [tsarah].
9.notes: vi-hi YHWH misgab la-dakh (H3068, H4869, H1790): a misgab -- the margin's 'high place', a fortress on a cliff -- for the dak, the crushed, the man ground down; misgab le-ittot ba-tsarah (H6256, H6869): a high place for the times when trouble comes. The Judge of verse 8 is the Refuge of verse 9: the same throne, seen from below.

10.text: Those who know Your name will trust in You, for You, LORD, have not abandoned those who seek You.
10.amp: And they that know [yada] Your name [shem] will put their trust [batach] in You: for You, LORD [YHWH], have not forsaken [azab] them that seek [darash] You.
10.notes: ve-yibtechu bekha yodee shemekha (H982, H3045, H8034): trust follows knowledge -- those who KNOW the Name trust the One who bears it; ki lo-azabta doreshekha YHWH (H5800, H1875, H3068): You have not abandoned Your seekers. darash, seek, and azab, forsake, are the two verbs of the whole relationship: they seek, He does not leave (cf. 2 Chronicles 15:2).

11.text: Make music to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; declare among the peoples the things He has done.
11.amp: Sing praises [zamar] to the LORD [YHWH], which dwells [yashab] in Zion [Tsiyyon]: declare [nagad] among the people [am] His doings [alilot -- deeds].
11.notes: zammeru la-YHWH yoshev Tsiyyon (H2167, H3068, H3427, H6726): the third yashab of the psalm -- He sat to judge (v. 4), He sits forever (v. 7), He sits in Zion: the eternal throne has a street address. haggidu ba-ammim alilotav (H5046, H5971, H5949): DECLARE His deeds among the peoples -- the missionary line, Israel's news for the nations.

12.text: For He who avenges blood remembers them; He has not forgotten the cry of the afflicted.
12.amp: When He makes inquisition [darash -- seeks out, requires] for blood [dam], He remembers [zakar] them: He forgets [shakach] not the cry of the humble ['afflicted', anav, the KJV margin].
12.notes: ki-doresh damim otam zakhar (H1875, H1818, H2142): the Seeker of blood -- the kinsman-avenger's role, Genesis 9:5's 'I will require' -- remembers THEM, the victims; lo-shakhach tsaaqat anavim (H7911, H6035): He has not forgotten the cry of the afflicted, the margin's word. Abel's blood was the first case (Genesis 4:10); every unpunished murder is still on the docket.

13.text: Be gracious to me, O LORD; see my affliction at the hands of those who hate me, You who lift me up from the gates of death,
13.amp: Have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon me, O LORD [YHWH]; consider [raah -- see] my trouble [oni -- affliction] which I suffer of them that hate [sane] me, You that lift me up [rum] from the gates [shaar] of death [mavet]:
13.notes: chonneni YHWH reeh onyi mi-soneai (H2603, H3068, H7200, H6040, H8130): grace, and a LOOK at what the haters have done -- meromemi mi-shaare mavet (H7311, H8179, H4194): You who lift me from death's GATES -- Sheol as a walled city with a gatehouse (cf. Isaiah 38:10; Matthew 16:18). The thanksgiving turns into petition mid-psalm; the vindicated man is still in danger.

14.text: so that I may recount all Your praise in the gates of the daughter of Zion, and exult in Your salvation.
14.amp: That I may show forth [saphar -- recount] all Your praise [tehillah] in the gates [shaar] of the daughter [bat] of Zion [Tsiyyon]: I will rejoice [gil -- exult] in Your salvation [yeshuah].
14.notes: asapperah kol-tehillatekha (H5608, H8416): the saphar of verse 1 again -- be-shaare bat-Tsiyyon (H8179, H1323, H6726): gates against gates -- lifted from the gates of death (v. 13) to testify in the gates of Zion's daughter, the city personified; agilah bi-shuatekha (H1523, H3444): exulting in Your yeshuah. Rescue is for reporting.

15.text: The nations have sunk into the pit they made; in the net they hid, their own foot is caught.
15.amp: The heathen [goy -- nations] are sunk down in the pit [shachat] that they made [asah]: in the net [resheth] which [zu] they hid [taman] is their own foot [regel] taken.
15.notes: tabeu goyim be-shachat asu (H1471, H7845, H6213): sunk in the shachat, the pit THEY made -- be-reshet-zu tamanu nilkedah raglam (H7568, H2098, H2934, H3920, H7272): in the net they hid, their own foot snagged. The boomerang justice of Psalm 7:15-16 and Haman's gallows (Esther 7:10): evil is self-trapping, and God lets it be.

16.text: The LORD has made Himself known; He has carried out judgment: the wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
16.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is known [yada] by the judgment [mishpat] which He executes [asah]: the wicked [rasha] is snared in the work [poal] of his own hands [kaph -- palms]. Higgaion ['Meditation', higgayon, the KJV margin]. Selah [Selah].
16.notes: noda YHWH mishpat asah (H3045, H3068, H4941, H6213): the LORD is KNOWN -- revealed -- by the judgment He performs; be-phoal kappav noqesh rasha (H6467, H3709, H7563): the wicked snared in his own handiwork. higgayon (H1902) -- the margin's 'Meditation'; the word means a murmuring, a low musical sound (Psalm 92:3) -- paired with Selah: stop, and let the instruments say it again.

17.text: The wicked will turn back to Sheol -- all the nations that forget God.
17.amp: The wicked [rasha] shall be turned [shub] into hell [sheol], and all the nations [goy] that forget God [Elohim].
17.notes: yashubu reshaim li-sheolah (H7725, H7563, H7585): the wicked RETURN to Sheol -- shub, as if the grave were where they came from -- kol-goyim shekheche Elohim (H1471, H430): all nations forgetting God. Not atheists -- forgetters. The opposite of verse 12, where God does not forget the afflicted: memory is the moral hinge of the psalm.

18.text: For the needy will not always be forgotten; the hope of the afflicted will not perish forever.
18.amp: For the needy [ebyon] shall not always [netsach -- forever] be forgotten [shakach]: the expectation [tikvah -- hope] of the poor [ani -- afflicted] shall not perish [abad] for ever [ad].
18.notes: ki lo la-netsach yishakhach ebyon (H5331, H7911, H34): not FOREVER forgotten -- the same la-netsach that finished the enemy in verse 6 now guards the needy's hope; tiqvat anavim tobad la-ad (H8615, H6035, H6, H5703): the tikvah of the afflicted -- the cord-word, Rahab's scarlet line (Joshua 2:18) -- will not perish. The poor may wait; they will not wait forever.

19.text: Arise, O LORD! Do not let mortal man prevail; let the nations be judged in Your presence.
19.amp: Arise [qum], O LORD [YHWH]; let not man [enosh -- mortal man] prevail [azaz]: let the heathen [goy -- nations] be judged [shaphat] in Your sight [panim].
19.notes: qumah YHWH al-yaoz enosh (H6965, H3068, H5810, H582): rise, and let ENOSH not grow strong -- enosh, man in his frailty, the word for humanity that reminds it of its mortality (Psalm 8:4); yishaphetu goyim al-panekha (H8199, H1471, H6440): let the nations be judged in front of Your face. The psalm's courtroom reconvenes for a global docket.

20.text: Put terror into them, O LORD; let the nations know that they are only human. Selah.
20.amp: Put [shith] them in fear [mora -- terror, dread], O LORD [YHWH]: that the nations [goy] may know [yada] themselves to be but men [enosh]. Selah [Selah].
20.notes: shitah YHWH morah lahem (H7896, H3068, H4172): set a mora on them, a terror -- yedeu goyim enosh hemmah (H3045, H1471, H582): let the nations KNOW they are enosh. The whole psalm's cure for imperial arrogance is a correct anthropology: they are mortals, and He sits forever (v. 7). Selah -- and Psalm 10 continues the acrostic without a title.
